You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure, and several recent issue reports that have been pre-filtered by an external semantic retrieval model (SBERT) to be the most relevant to this failure among recent reports.

Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failing test `NumericEntityUnescaperTest.testUnfinishedEntity` is calling the `translate` method of `NumericEntityUnescaper` with an input containing an unfinished numeric entity "&#x30". This input is missing the semicolon at the end, causing a `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` at index 4 when trying to unescape the entity. The exception is thrown in the `translate` method of `NumericEntityUnescaper` at line 49, where it attempts to access a character beyond the length of the input string.

The root cause of the issue is the incomplete numeric entity in the input string, which results in the exception due to incorrect parsing or processing in the `translate` method of `NumericEntityUnescaper`.

The recent bug reports mention encoding or processing issues related to strings and characters, which align with the problem observed in the failing test case.

Next, I will suggest the methods that need to be fixed to address this issue.

The `NumericEntityUnescaper.translate` method attempts to process numeric entities in the input string. The method starts by checking for the presence of `&#` in the input, followed by parsing the numeric value and writing the corresponding character to an output writer. 

In this case, the issue is likely occurring due to the incomplete handling of the numeric entity when the entity is not properly terminated with a semicolon (`;`). This incomplete entity leads to the `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` when trying to parse the entity value.

To address this issue, the `NumericEntityUnescaper.translate` method should be modified to handle cases where the numeric entity is not terminated correctly with a semicolon. The parsing logic should be adjusted to account for such scenarios to prevent index out of range errors.

The following method should be fixed:
```
org.apache.commons.lang3.text.translate.NumericEntityUnescaper.translate(java.lang.CharSequence, int, java.io.Writer)
```

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
